note: Optionale Funde und Gespräche in Kapitel 3 (data/explore/veltrava_station.json, veltrava_hall.json). Fundtexte werden als Gedanke der Spielfigur gesprochen (höchstens 230 Zeichen). Bahnhof = Alexei: kurze Fragen, genaue Beobachtungen, trockener Humor, nie zynisch gegenüber Opfern. Palais = Konrad: längere, genaue Sätze, anfangs beschönigend, zunehmend direkt. Zitate in gesprochenen Zeilen mit ‚…‘.

strings.explore.veltrava.station.footprints.text: Under the platform edge, fresh footprints in the snow, several pairs. They lead over the edge down into the track bed and disappear under carriage two. Whoever walks this way passes no counter. Who is showing them the way?
strings.explore.veltrava.station.four_rails.text: Four rails in one track: standard gauge and our broad gauge. The gauges are too close together to share a rail, so each has its own pair. Neither side has to give way – not even by 89 millimetres.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_voronova.t: The minister counts grain trains and coal wagons. Annex C she leaves to the lawyers. Until recently I counted that way too.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_voronova.l: Morozov, good that you’re here. Tomorrow you explain every set of points at Kordon-17 to the Reich delegation. Your opinion of it, you tell me first.
If the corridors hold, grain trains will reach Karsk in the autumn. Bread, Morozov. I need no more politics than that.
Annex C? Logistics. The lawyers handle that.
Tell me instead whether the coal in Karsk will last until spring. On my desk are letters from mothers, not from ministers.
Until March. If no more wagons disappear.
Then make sure none disappear. That’s why I brought you.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.luggage.title: Case with wooden horse
strings.explore.veltrava.station.luggage.text: A delegation suitcase, tied up and numbered. On top, a wooden horse, strapped down with a trouser belt. Who takes a toy to a conference? Someone who isn’t travelling alone.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.pigeons.title: Negotiations among pigeons
strings.explore.veltrava.station.pigeons.text: Two pigeons tug at a sandwich from the delegation’s provisions. A third waits at the edge until both are exhausted, then eats. I suspect it’s from the Commission.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.bogie.title: The bogies of wagon 4
strings.explore.veltrava.station.bogie.text: Under wagon four: gauge-changing bogies, freshly greased. The wagon runs on both gauges without being reloaded. Someone has made sure it fits any train – and that nobody has to open the door.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.mitten.title: A single mitten
strings.explore.veltrava.station.mitten.text: A single mitten on the bench, laid out neatly so its owner will find it. There was one in Karsk too. Perhaps they follow the trains.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.clock.title: Three clocks
strings.explore.veltrava.station.clock.text: Three clocks side by side: Veltrava, Moscow, Berlin. Each one is right, none agrees with the others. They agree only on the minutes.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.kiosk.title: Three front pages
strings.explore.veltrava.station.kiosk.text: The same photo on three front pages. From Moscow: ‘Victory for the policy of peace’. From Berlin: ‘German order on every track’. In the city paper: ‘Frost until Thursday’. Only the weather report can be checked.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.poster.title: The Commission’s poster
strings.explore.veltrava.station.poster.text: The Commission’s poster says ‘Three corridors – one peace’. It’s not a year old and already coming loose. Someone has pinned one corner with a drawing pin. The other three hang.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.te: The border official distrusts everyone equally and takes pains over it. In Veltrava that may be the politest form of justice.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.l1: You said everyone here is a foreigner. You too?
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.l2: I was born here. My father wasn’t, my wife wasn’t, my superior wasn’t either. In Veltrava that’s the rule.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.l3: So I distrust everyone equally. Germans, Russians, neutrals. Most of all, papers that look too good.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.l5: No. They looked genuine. Somebody always writes something into genuine papers without asking.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.l6: My daughter learns three languages at school. In the evenings she explains to me what my stamps say.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.chat_officer.l7: Take care of yourself, Herr Morozov. And if anyone offers you better papers: don’t buy any.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.return_notice.t: A notice in three languages from the ‘Office for Repatriation’: persons without valid corridor papers are to report to Room 4. Repatriation. A word that sounds like going home.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.stove.title: Tiled stove in the waiting room
strings.explore.veltrava.station.stove.text: A tiled stove in the waiting room; the porters are warming their hands. In the coal scuttle, coal from Karsk lies beside briquettes from the Reich. The stove doesn’t ask for papers.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.exchange.title: Bureau de change
strings.explore.veltrava.station.exchange.text: The bureau de change: Reichsmark, rouble, Veltrava crown. The rates are chalked on the board, corrected three times. Only the crown knows what it’s worth.
strings.explore.veltrava.station.tram.title: Trilingual route sign
strings.explore.veltrava.station.tram.text: Outside the exit the tram is waiting. The route sign is handwritten, in three languages: Station – Palace – Old Town. Here at least, three languages say the same thing.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.flags.title: Six flags
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.flags.text: Six flags, of equal height and equally spaced; I measured out of habit. Protocol is said to have wrestled over two centimetres for weeks. At a scale of 1:100 that would be the thickness of a pencil line.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.cloakroom.title: Cloakroom
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.cloakroom.text: The coats of both delegations hang hook by hook, loden beside karakul, with no seating plan at all. Among them, a dark grey woman’s coat with a wine-red scarf. Nobody goes out without a coat in this weather.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.photos.title: Photo wall, 1953
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.photos.text: The photo wall: March 1953, the signing of the armistice, here in this building. The gentlemen at the table look relieved or exhausted. After fourteen winters of war, the picture shows mainly fountain pens.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.te: Ekdahl gave me his card. I did not put it in my folder but in my coat pocket. I could not say exactly why.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l1: Nils Ekdahl, I write for a Stockholm paper. You’re the Reich delegation’s draughtsman? A sentence for my readers?
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l2: The delegation speaks through its spokesman. I am merely responsible for the technical documents.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l3: Then a technical sentence. What is being built at Kordon-17?
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l4: A transhipment facility with the necessary ancillary rooms, within the framework of the agreed logistics integration.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l5: Word for word as in the communiqué. – Here’s my card. If you ever draw something that isn’t right, call me.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l6: Suppose I did. What would it change?
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_journalist.l7: Perhaps nothing. A newspaper doesn’t stop a train. But it writes down that it ran.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chandelier.title: Chandelier
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chandelier.text: The Commission, so they say, bought the chandelier’s crystals in equal parts in three countries. One, unless I am mistaken, is the polished bottom of a beer bottle. It sparkles most beautifully.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.buffet.title: Untouched buffet
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.buffet.text: Sekt from the Reich, caviar from the Soviet Union, cheese from Switzerland – all untouched. Whoever reached first would presumably have given way first. At home people queue for margarine.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.window.title: View of the Line
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.window.text: Beyond the window the frozen river, and on the far bank, at regular intervals, the watchtowers of the Line. From here they look like survey points. They are not.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.evac_plan.title: Escape route plan
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.evac_plan.text: Others read letters; I read escape route plans. This one shows a staff corridor that appears in no visitors’ plan and leads down to a cellar archive. In case of fire, after all, no room may be missing.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.treaty_shelf.title: Border treaties 1919–1953
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.treaty_shelf.text: Bound border treaties from 1919 to 1953, one volume per year, gold lettering on the spine. 1939 stands between 1938 and 1940, as if it were a year like any other.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.title: Conversation with Frau Brunner
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.text: Frau Brunner types every session three times. Frau Weiss writes every note twice, by hand, and trusts no carbon copy. Today her coat is hanging downstairs in the cloakroom.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l1: Minutes office, Brunner. German, Russian, French – I type every session three times, with two carbons each.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l2: Then the three versions presumably match down to the last comma.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l3: They match down to the comma when I’ve finished. Seldom before.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l4: Only Fräulein Weiss never gives me anything to type. She writes her notes by hand, and everything twice at that.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l5: Twice by hand? A carbon copy would be more accurate; it can’t make a slip of the pen.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l6: That’s what I told her. She says anyone can read a carbon copy.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.chat_typist.l7: And today she left her coat downstairs – in this weather. Usually she keeps it on even in the booth.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.mimeograph.title: Duplicator
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.mimeograph.text: Wax stencils in three languages hang on the duplicator; beside it, a basket of carbon paper, black as ink. Held up to the light, every sheet could be read. Usually such things are burned.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.headsets.title: Interpreters’ headphones
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.headsets.text: In front of the booths lie headphones with a selector switch from 1 to 4. One turn, and every delegation hears the session in its own language. Whether they understand what was meant, no switch decides.
